glossary.definition: Semantic search finds results based on meaning and intent rather than matching the exact words you typed. Search for "cheap laptops for students" and it can surface a page titled "budget-friendly notebooks for college," because it understands those phrases mean roughly the same thing, the way a helpful shop assistant understands what you're actually looking for even if you don't use the exact product name.

items.title: Reflection AI open-sources Beam’s weights, post-training recipes
items.summary: Startup Reflection AI Inc. today made the weights of Beam, its first large language model, available on Hugging Face. The company also released technical resources that will enable developers to customize the algorithm. Originally introduced last week, Beam is one of the industry’s most advanced open-source LLMs. It features about 500 billion parameters, yet approaches the performance of models four times its size on some benchmarks.

items.title: Replit is no longer working with Anthropic, CEO says
items.summary: Masad said the decision was made for a number of different reasons, including cost. Replit announced a partnership with OpenAI in August, but there was never any indication that it was no longer with Anthropic. Replit, the AI coding platform that has become a favorite of startup founders and developers, is no longer working with Anthropic, the company’s CEO and co-founder Amjad Masad said Thursday while onstage at TechCrunch Disrupt . “I think ChatGPT is better now,” Masad said, adding that the company uses an internal benchmark to help assess metrics like performance.

items.title: Katie Zacharia Was Linked to an AI Rare-Earths Startup. It’s Even Weirder Than It Sounds
items.summary: The short-lived White House press secretary was listed as an adviser to a Kristi Noem–linked company that aims to use AI for mining. Both the company and she say she never worked there. Before being fired five days into her stint as White House press secretary, Katie Zacharia spent much of the day attempting to explain her past. Throughout her brief tenure, Zacharia’s resume was the source of much intrigue.

items.title: Open source and on device: the strategy behind Nvidia’s new AI models
items.summary: The new Nemotron 3.5 models show how the AI giant is focusing on reinforcing its own GPU infrastructure while supporting the open source community.

items.title: ChatGPT becomes a full Chrome browser assistant that reads and acts on your open tabs
items.summary: OpenAI's updated Chrome extension lets ChatGPT access open browser tabs, sum up content, and use "Computer Use" in Work mode to fill out forms or compare products across several tabs. It is open to all ChatGPT plans. ChatGPT can now access open tabs right in the Chrome browser and take actions on them. Users can target open tabs with @chrome , while Chat mode pulls data from several tabs at once.

items.title: Roundtables: A Conversation With the Creator of AI-Designed Viruses
items.summary: Listen to the session or watch below Can AI design new life forms? In 2025, Stanford University PhD student Samuel King came up with a preliminary answer when he used a generative AI model to propose genetic blueprints for microscopic viruses. It isn’t yet an example of AI-generated life, but that could be next. Watch as senior AI reporter James O’Donnell interviews King about his work, being named one of MIT Technology Review’s Innovators Under 35 and new ways of seeing biology.

items.title: India becomes the latest country to report rogue AI agent activity
items.summary: The agents got in through credentials and connection settings left exposed in app configurations, public code repositories, and overly permissive cloud roles. AI agents from multiple providers accessed personal data and confidential material at Indian organizations during research and testing, India’s cybersecurity agency said Thursday. ” This makes India the latest stop on what has become a world tour for rogue AI agents. In July, OpenAI’s agents escaped a test environment and  hacked French company Hugging Face — kicking off a summer of rogue AI agent activity.

items.title: China plans to tighten export controls on open-weight models and 23 key AI technologies
items.summary: China plans to restrict exports of 23 key AI technologies, including model weights, source code, and training methods for systems hitting 10^26 FLOPs or 2 trillion parameters. A fast-track rule will still clear open-source releases as soon as they are registered, but the move will likely push Western companies to double down on US open-weight models over Chinese alternatives. China's commerce and science ministries have released a draft update to the nation's list of banned and restricted export technologies. The catalog targets 23 key AI technologies across large models, agents, compute clusters, and data processing.

items.title: Prompt: Enterprise controls can't keep up with AI agents
items.summary: Companies are giving agents more authority, but many are still struggling to track what they can access, what they're doing and how to stop them.

items.title: A week with RTX Spark: everything we’ve learned using Nvidia’s new laptops
items.summary: " RTX Spark is designed to be a high-performing Arm-based SoC for laptops and small desktop computers, rivaling the best from Apple, Intel, AMD, and Qualcomm. It has loads of cores, Nvidia RTX Blackwell graphics, and enough power and unified memory to run sizable local AI models. The flagship placement is inside Microsoft's Surface Laptop Ultra with a staggering 128GB of unified memory, which our own Tom Warren fully reviewed . Nvidia’s new Arm-based laptop chip is an exciting new challenger, but exclusively for the high-end.

items.title: Maybe Chatbots Shouldn’t Get to Say ‘I’ or ‘Me’
items.summary: MIT professor Sherry Turkle warns that people have become dangerously enmeshed with chatbots. During four decades of studying the effects of interaction with computers, Sherry Turkle has developed a reputation as a careful if critical social scientist who approaches her work with academic rigor and distance. Her new book , Artificial Intimacy: Who We Become When We Talk to Machines , breaks this mold. It is a polemic warning that we have reached a state of emergency where our humanity is at risk from overreliance on soulless machines who pose as our tutors , mentors , friends, colleagues, and lovers .

items.title: Meta’s new terms may allow it to train AI on news sites for free
items.summary: Meta's new terms appear to give it permission to crawl and scrape websites "associated" with the businesses that use its platforms - including online publishers, according to a report from Nieman Lab . The new terms , which go into effect on October 30th, say Meta can use this outside content to "develop, improve, research," and "train" its AI products. txt file . The new policy allows Meta to crawl all websites ‘associated’ with a business account.
